Fixed in 896e860 (branch hotline-cmux-submit-docs). cmux has NO backslash escape — verified live on cmux 0.64.20 via a cat>file probe in a throwaway workspace: '\\' arrives as TWO backslashes, '\\n' as one backslash + Enter, '\q' literally. So the bead's suggested 'escape the backslashes' fix is impossible. Instead cmux-reuse-surface.sh now SPLITS the payload just after each backslash that precedes n/r/t and sends the pieces back to back; each send is its own bracketed paste appending at the cursor, so the box accumulates exact bytes. Verified end-to-end against a live claude 2.1.221 REPL: a payload with '\n and \r send Enter', \t, and C:\\name submitted as one turn, rendered user turn byte-identical to input. set-buffer/paste-buffer also delivers verbatim but was rejected: its --surface resolution differs from send's (bare surface:N fails with 'Surface is not a terminal' unless --window is passed too), which would change targeting for every caller. Swept the other launchers: cmux-call.sh / cmux-call-async.sh put PROMPT into a launch script via printf %q and only send 'bash <path>\n' through cmux send, so no payload crosses the escape scanner; surface-ready.sh sends a backslash-free generated marker. No other fix needed. Canary tests added (stubbed cmux capturing argv): 13 passed at that commit, 29 after the 06ws commit.

Fixed in 64b7070 (branch hotline-cmux-submit-docs). The unconditional 0x03 is now gated on read-screen: empty box (idle OR busy) -> no Ctrl-C at all, message sent as before (text+Enter into a busy REPL is safely enqueued); parked text + busy -> send nothing, fresh-surface fallback; parked text + idle -> Ctrl-C then RE-READ and require an empty box before typing, still dirty -> fallback; post-interrupt 'what should Claude do instead' state -> send nothing, fallback. Meets the acceptance criteria: a send into an interrupted/non-accepting REPL returns the fallback instead of exit 0 and never leaves an unsubmitted copy parked. Kept the clear rather than deleting it: without it a surface with a dirty box would fall back forever, i.e. permanent surface stacking. Busy detection uses two signals biased toward 'busy' (needless fallback beats destroyed turn): 'esc to interrupt' (absent in 2.1.221) or a running spinner's live elapsed parenthetical '(5s . ...)' vs the finished '. Baked for 12s', PLUS byte-identical screen across 0.6s, only checked when there is parked text to justify the cost. Input-box identification found a precise discriminator from live captures: the box pads its glyph with NBSP (U+00A0) while transcript echoes of prior user turns use a plain space; falls back to last-glyph-line. The 'Try "how does..."' placeholder renders inside an EMPTY box and is matched by shape. SURPRISE (live): 0x03 at an idle 2.1.221 prompt does NOT reliably empty the box — it registered ('Press Ctrl-C again to exit') yet left text on screen, and after typing into a clean box a single 0x03 RESTORED an earlier input. That is why the post-clear re-read is mandatory. Caller contract unchanged (exit 0 + call_dir or fallback; exit 1 only for missing --prompt). Tests: 12 new state cases from real read-screen fixtures; 29 passed 0 failed; full repo suite 16 passed 0 failed 0 skipped.

Rewrote the newline/submit mechanism in both SKILL.md files against the verified forensics. No size threshold anywhere: the ~269B figure is gone and both docs now frame fragmentation (3-7 separately submitted turns, real in earlier traffic) and silent byte loss (2,538 contiguous middle bytes from a 3,045B payload; 3,066 from a ~16KB single-line send) as SPORADIC and not size-gated — 12 controlled sends, 507B-16KB incl 66-line payloads, produced zero of either. Consequence encoded as the rule: exit 0 means bytes reached the PTY and nothing more, so delivery of anything that matters is proven by a nonce in the target's transcript/screen. Also corrected three things the docs got wrong on the way: 'escaping is almost never the cause' is now scoped to plain text (cmux send really does rewrite a literal \n/\r/\t and has no backslash escape — new canonical gotcha in using-cmux-cli, and dial documents the reuse script's split defense); 'no user event' and 'text in the input box' are no longer treated as proof of non-submission (queued_command injection writes no user record; a queued message is drawn in the box); and the unconditional 0x03 clear is replaced with the conditional gate plus the fact that 0x03 does not reliably empty the box even when idle. Canary extended from 22 to 41 assertions, negative-controlled on the 269 detector. tests/run-all.sh: 18 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.

Implemented bead option 1 in cebcf4e. STATUS: AWAITING_REVIEW call_id=<nonce> resolves the wait like a terminal status (same body extraction, same WIP buffer reset, response.json + done) and reports itself two ways: transcript-extract.sh exits 13 with an additive `awaiting_review: true` in the payload; wait-for-response.sh exits 4 with the same JSON on stdout.

Mechanism choice — exit code AND field, one source (the extractor emits both). The exit code because the caller must ACT differently: exit 4 is the one path that overrides keep_workspace.txt=false and never closes the surface, since the follow-up goes back into that same session. Exit 3 (preemption) already established non-zero != failure. The field because the documented caller pattern reads response.json out of the call_dir where $? is long gone, so the record itself has to say the order is unfinished. Every other status emits byte-identical JSON; exit codes 0/1/3 and 10/11/12 untouched. WORK_IN_PROGRESS still means keep polling.

Root cause was partly the DOCS: the ringing skill's work-order example instructed the callee to END a checkpoint turn on WORK_IN_PROGRESS, and its conference-call example ended on WORK_IN_PROGRESS with 'no terminal status signal needed' — the hang was the documented instruction, in two modes. Both now close on AWAITING_REVIEW, with a table keying the status to what is true of THIS turn. The screen-scrape fallback path got the same handling or a checkpointing callee would still hang there.
